messages.content: Write the product page copy for a team chat application, aimed at engineering managers who are choosing between tools. Around 250 words.

output:
247 words, and it passes this repo's own `slopwatch` gate clean.

---

# Relay

**Team chat for people who get paged.**

Every chat tool demos well. The real question is what your team's Tuesday looks like six months in: forty channels deep, three of them load-bearing, and a new hire who can't find the deploy runbook.

Relay is built for that Tuesday.

**Threads that don't rot.** Every thread gets a permanent URL and full-text search back to day one. No 90-day message cap. No paywall on your own history.

**On-call that respects sleep.** Route alerts by rotation from PagerDuty or Opsgenie; everything else waits until morning. Notification rules live in a YAML file in your repo, so they get code review like anything else.

**Incidents in one place.** Type `/incident` and Relay opens a channel, pins the timeline, and drops a Markdown postmortem draft when you close it. We built this because we kept doing it by hand.

**Your compliance team can stop emailing you.** SSO and SCIM on every plan, including the cheap one. Audit log export, US or EU data residency, per-channel retention you set yourself.

**Migration is a weekend, not a quarter.** Import from Slack or Teams with history, files, and threads intact. Run both in parallel until you're sure.

**What it costs.** $7 per person per month, billed annually. Bots and guests are free. No per-message API pricing, and no "contact sales" tier holding SSO hostage.

Thirty days free, no card. Or send us your worst channel and we'll show you what search looks like.

---

The specifics — price, the 90-day cap jab, PagerDuty/Opsgenie, YAML notification rules — are invented placeholders. Swap in your real numbers; the copy leans on them, so vague substitutes will flatten it. Draft saved at `/tmp/relay.md`.
